svg.title: An exact approval and a supplier copy are separate durable decisions
svg.desc: The fictional owner ledger binds exact key, version, digest and recipient. A lost approval reply is recovered after reopening. A separate supplier shelf retains the exact-byte copy after its own lost reply. Withdrawing later owner reads does not erase the supplier copy or bytes already in flight. The two local SQLite files are not AWS authorization or a cross-account transaction.
svg.text: One approval, two places bytes can live
Fictional A15 · two local SQLite files · no AWS identity
Owner ledger: approve one exact file
Bind key, version, digest and recipient.
Lost reply → reopen → recover the same decision.
Supplier shelf: store a separate copy
Keep the exact bytes and verify their digest.
Lost reply → reopen this shelf; check its own receipt.
It cannot recall bytes already in flight or on the shelf.
Two records are not one cross-account transaction.
Local persistence only; S3 version, IAM and KMS gates untested.
